text:
alex_m: FYI customer reported a big latency regression after we enabled a new quant profile for model rw-infer-v2. p95 jumped from ~85ms -> ~420ms, p99 from ~240ms -> ~1.1s. They're on dedicated capacity and started seeing 5xx retries and timeouts.
raj: thanks — do we know which profile was flipped? int8-only or fp8 hybrid?
jess: looks like ops toggled the int8-calibrated-profile (auto-fp8 disabled). change rolled at 02:14 UTC.
carla: customer claim also mentioned an auth error intermittently (401) around the same window, could be unrelated rate limiting?
mike: checked logs: majority of slow traces show heavy long-seq requests (seq_len > 2048) and lots of KV cache misses. kernel selected was int8-kernel-v3 which has different chunking behavior.
alex_m: reproducible on our side with their prompt set: can repro p99 high when using the int8 profile, not when forcing fp16.
raj: can you paste the minimal repro command?
jess: repro script:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rw-infer-v2","quant_profile":"int8-calib-2027-02","inputs":[{"text":"<long prompt repeated...>","max_tokens":1024}]}'
```
carla: ran that locally, p95 ~380ms p99 ~1.05s. forcing `quant_profile: fp16` drops p99 back to ~180ms.
mike: hypothesis: calibration stage produced suboptimal kernel path for long sequences causing more per-token overhead and breaking some batching optimizations. also noticed extra memcpy on GPU in traces.
raj: short mitigations we can do now? customer needs immediate relief.
alex_m: applied emergency rollback for that customer's tenant to use fp16 variant at 03:01 UTC. they confirmed latency dropped and retries stopped.
jess: action: enable runtime fallback rule -> if model runtime selects int8 path and request > 1024 tokens or latency > 350ms then route to fp16 variant. we can gate it per-tenant.
mike: created canary job to rerun calibration with longer warmup (10k steps) and sequence-length aware sampling. also added a KV-cache sanity check in runtime to avoid cache misses caused by half-precision rounding.
carla: billing/auth note: the 401 spikes were due to their token hitting per-minute rate limits because clients retried on timeouts. support advised them to disable aggressive retry while we rollback. billing should check for accidental overage; I'll open ticket to Billing for potential credit.
raj: longer term: add quant profile smoke tests that include long-seq prompts and p95/p99 thresholds before rollout. also add an A/B canary flag for new quant profiles.
alex_m: created incident ticket INC-2027-58, tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml. owners: mike (eng-runtime) and jess (eng-ml).
sre_bot: deploy notice: rollback of quant profile for tenant 12345 completed at 03:01 UTC by alex_m.
mike: next steps: 1) run extended calibration job and record kernel choices, 2) add automatic fallback policy, 3) update rollout playbook to include p95/p99 gate and sequence-length tests. I'll push PR for the fallback rule this morning.
jess: will re-run evals comparing quality delta int8 vs fp16 on customer prompt set to ensure fallbacks don't degrade output. if quality drop > 3% we'll adjust retrain/calibration.
carla: support message to customer: "We've rolled back the quant profile for your tenant and implemented a temporary fallback to fp16 for long requests. We're running a safe recalibration and will follow up with timeline. Sorry for the disruption." :heart:
alex_m: thanks all. I'll update the customer thread and close once recalibration is validated.
